rows.grounds: bindu having the form of space
half of that is the half-moon, by an eighth of that

items.question: How are the subtle sound units from bindu to nirodhikā defined?
premises: The half-measure is taught as bindu in the form of space.
Bindu is described as having four kalas.
Half of bindu is the half-moon, and by an eighth of that comes nirodhikā.
items.inference: The verse maps a descending sequence of subtle sound measures from bindu through half-moon to nirodhikā.
uncertainties: The exact mathematical parsing of tadardhamardhacandrastadaṣṭāṃśena is compressed and may allow slight variation.
items.plain_english: The half-measure is called bindu, which has the form of space and four phases. Half of that is the half-moon, and by an eighth part of that comes nirodhikā.

rows.grounds: the causal lords starting with Brahma
one should leave it after that

items.question: What must be transcended to reach the supreme Sadakhya world?
premises: Rodhikā obstructs the causal lords beginning with Brahma.
That rodhikā should be abandoned.
After piercing this nirodhikā one reaches the supreme Sadakhya world.
items.inference: Spiritual ascent requires passing beyond rodhikā and nirodhikā to attain Sadakhya.
uncertainties: The subject of tyajet is implicit, likely the practitioner.
items.plain_english: Rodhikā blocks the causal lords beginning with Brahma; one should abandon it. Then, after piercing this nirodhikā, one reaches the supreme world called Sadakhya.

rows.grounds: having a great body of five mantras
thus, above the covering of bindu ending in half-moon and nirodhi

items.question: What great reality abides above bindu ending in half-moon and nirodhi?
premises: In Sadakhya abides one with a great body of five mantras.
He abides there in a supreme form.
Above the covering of bindu ending in half-moon and nirodhi there is a great reality.
items.inference: Beyond the bindu sequence, in supreme form, dwells the great five-mantra-bodied lord.
uncertainties: The compound ityardhendunirodhyantabindvāvṛtyūrdhvato is dense and its internal boundaries are interpretive.
items.plain_english: There, in supreme form, abides the one whose great body is made of the five mantras. Thus, above the covering of bindu that ends in the half-moon and nirodhi, there is a great presence.

items.question: How is nāda described and how are its worlds arranged?
premises: Nāda is like flower filaments and surrounded by great beings.
There are four worlds there in the directions.
There is a fifth world in the middle.
items.inference: Nāda is a populated subtle realm arranged with four directional worlds and one central world.
items.plain_english: Nāda is like the filaments of a flower and is surrounded by great beings. There are four worlds in the directions and a fifth in the center.

items.question: Which powers and central form are present in the nāda realm?
premises: Indhikā, Dīpikā, Rodhikā, and upward-going Mocikā are present.
In the middle there is a lotus.
There the upward-moving one is surrounded by its śaktis.
items.inference: The nāda realm contains four named powers around a central lotus with an upward-moving presence attended by śaktis.
uncertainties: The identity of the upward-moving one is not explicitly named in this verse.
items.plain_english: Indhikā, Dīpikā, Rodhikā, and the upward-going Mocikā are there. In the middle is a lotus, and there the upward-moving one is surrounded by its powers.

rows.grounds: the lord who bears its śaktis
on the left and right sides

items.question: What lies above nāda and how is its lord attended?
premises: Above nāda is the suṣumna realm.
There the lord bears its śaktis.
That lord is surrounded on left and right by Piṅgalā and Iḍā.
items.inference: The suṣumna level above nāda is ruled by a lord attended by śaktis and flanked by Piṅgalā and Iḍā.
items.plain_english: Above nāda is the suṣumna realm. There the lord who bears its powers is surrounded on the left and right by Piṅgalā and Iḍā.

items.question: How does Suṣumnā structure the entire path above and below?
premises: The goddess Suṣumnā rests in the lord's lap and shines like the moon.
By her the whole path is strung together.
This includes both the upper and the lower regions.
items.inference: Suṣumnā is the unifying channel that binds the entire vertical path.
items.plain_english: The goddess Suṣumnā, resting in the lord's lap and shining like the moon, strings together the whole path, both above and below.

rows.grounds: but the support of nāda and suṣumnā
goes forth by the upward śakti

items.question: How does the nāda-suṣumnā support pervade and exit the universe?
premises: The support of nāda and suṣumnā pierces this entire universe.
It goes out below by the downward śakti.
It goes out above from the crown by the upward śakti.
items.inference: The nāda-suṣumnā axis permeates the whole cosmos and extends beyond it in both directions.
items.plain_english: The support of nāda and suṣumnā pierces this entire universe; it goes out below by the downward power and above from the crown by the upward power.

items.question: What is the nature of the unmanifest sound absorbed in the brahma cavity?
premises: Through the channel it is absorbed in the cavity of Brahma.
It is unmanifest, resonant, and imperishable.
It resounds in all beings, presided over by Śiva's śakti.
items.inference: The subtle imperishable sound abides in the brahma cavity yet pervades all beings through Śiva's śakti.
items.plain_english: Absorbed through the channel in the cavity of Brahma, that unmanifest, resonant, imperishable sound resounds in all beings, empowered by Śiva's śakti.

rows.grounds: the covering known as the brahma cavity

items.question: Who resides in the covering called the brahma cavity above Suṣumnā?
premises: Above Suṣumnā is the covering known as the brahma cavity.
There resides Brahmā.
He is described as white, three-eyed, trident-bearing, five-faced, and moon-crested.
items.inference: The brahma cavity above Suṣumnā is inhabited by a Brahmā depicted with Śaiva attributes.
uncertainties: The Śaiva iconography applied to Brahmā here is unusual and may reflect a specific tantric identification.
items.plain_english: Above Suṣumnā is the covering called the brahma cavity. There dwells Brahmā, white, three-eyed, bearing a trident, five-faced, and crowned with the moon.

rows.grounds: moving on the path of liberation

items.question: What role does Brahmāṇī play and what lies beyond her?
premises: In Brahmā's lap sits the supreme goddess Brahmāṇī on the path of liberation.
She both obstructs and grants liberation.
After piercing her, one reaches the upward Kuṇḍalinī.
items.inference: Brahmāṇī is a threshold power who can block or grant liberation, beyond whom Kuṇḍalinī rises.
items.plain_english: In his lap sits the supreme goddess Brahmāṇī, who moves on the path of liberation and both obstructs and grants release. Piercing through her, one comes to the upward Kuṇḍalinī.

items.question: How is Kuṇḍalinī described and what powers reside within her?
premises: Kuṇḍalinī is a śakti like a sleeping serpent.
She is called the support of the universe.
Within her are Sūkṣmā, Susūkṣmā, Amṛtā, Amitā, and others.
items.inference: Kuṇḍalinī is the cosmic support containing a hierarchy of increasingly subtle śaktis.
uncertainties: The verse names some śaktis explicitly but leaves others unspecified as 'others'.
items.plain_english: That śakti is like a sleeping serpent and is called the support of the universe. Within her are the subtle, the very subtle, Amṛtā, Amitā, and other powers.

items.question: What is the śakti principle and how far does its manifestation extend?
premises: In the middle is Vyāpinī, and within her is Vyāpīśa, the bearer of Vyāpinī.
This is the śakti principle.
Its manifestation extends all the way down to earth.
items.inference: The śakti principle, centered in Vyāpinī and Vyāpīśa, unfolds as the entire cosmos down to the earth level.
items.plain_english: In the middle is Vyāpinī, and within her is Vyāpīśa, the bearer of Vyāpinī. This is the śakti principle, whose manifestation extends all the way down to earth.

rows.grounds: the sky-natured Ananta lord and those sharing his śaktis

items.question: What appears at the Śiva principle and who is established there?
premises: Beyond that is the Śiva principle.
In the four directions are established beings.
There are Vyāpī, the sky-natured Ananta lord, and those who share his śaktis.
items.inference: At the Śiva principle level, Vyāpī and the sky-natured Ananta with associated śaktis are established in the four directions.
uncertainties: The compound at the end is compressed; the exact grouping of Ananta and the śakti-sharers is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Then comes the Śiva principle. Established in the four directions are Vyāpī, the sky-natured lord Ananta, and those who share in his powers.

rows.grounds: bearing its śakti in his lap, radiant like a hundred crore suns

items.question: Who is the unsupported lord at the center of the Śiva principle?
premises: In the middle is the unsupported reality.
There is the god of gods, indeed the unsupported one.
He bears his śakti in his lap and shines like a hundred crore suns.
items.inference: The center of the Śiva principle is occupied by Anāśrita Śiva, radiant and united with his śakti.
items.plain_english: In the middle there is the unsupported one: the god of gods, Anāśrita, bearing his śakti in his lap and shining with the radiance of a hundred crore suns.

items.question: What supreme śakti abides above the Śiva principle and what is her role?
premises: Above the Śiva principle is the supreme śakti.
She is called Samanā.
She abides as the agent of all causes.
items.inference: Samanā is the supreme causal agency operating above the Śiva principle.
items.plain_english: Above the Śiva principle is the supreme śakti called Samanā. She abides as the active agent of all causes.

items.question: How do Samanā and Śiva function together in cosmic activity?
premises: Empowered by Śiva, Samanā bears many cosmic eggs.
Śiva, mounted upon her, is the lord.
He performs the five acts.
items.inference: Samanā supports the cosmos while Śiva, acting through her, performs the five cosmic functions.
items.plain_english: Empowered by Śiva, she bears many cosmic eggs. Resting upon her, Lord Śiva performs the five acts.

rows.grounds: of the causal agent, the great lord

items.question: How are Samanā and the unsupported principle classified as causes?
premises: Samanā is the instrument of the great causal lord.
The unsupported principle functions in activity as the occasioning cause.
That unsupported principle is called the cause.
items.inference: Samanā serves as instrument, while the unsupported Śiva principle is the ultimate occasioning cause.
items.plain_english: Samanā is the instrument of that great causal lord. The unsupported principle, in activity, is the occasioning cause and is called the cause.

items.question: How does the all-pervading lord govern the five causes?
premises: Through Samanā the all-pervading lord presides over the five causes.
He is unsupported, lordly, endless, and sky-bodied.
He abides thus always.
items.inference: The eternal unsupported lord governs the fivefold causal system through Samanā.
uncertainties: The identity of the five causes is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Through her the all-pervading lord presides over the five causes. This unsupported, lordly, endless, sky-bodied one does so always.

items.question: How does the lord set the lower cosmic process in motion?
premises: He impels the pervading lord by his own śakti as instrument.
Below that abides Māyā in the form of karma.
Below that is the śakti Kuṇḍalinī.
items.inference: The supreme lord initiates manifestation through his śakti, leading down to Māyā and Kuṇḍalinī.
items.plain_english: He impels the pervading lord by his own śakti as instrument. Below that abides Māyā in the form of karma, and below that is the śakti Kuṇḍalinī.

rows.grounds: the arising of the world beginning thus as effect

items.question: What range of manifestation is described as effect in the teaching?
premises: The arising of the world begins as effect with nāda, bindu, and so on.
In the teaching this range extends up to Sadāśiva.
It also includes what begins with the earthly level.
items.inference: The scriptural teaching treats the whole manifest range, from subtle nāda-bindu down to earth and up to Sadāśiva, as produced effect.
uncertainties: The verse is syntactically compressed and continues the thought from the previous verse.
items.plain_english: The arising of the world as effect begins with nāda, bindu, and so on. In the teaching, this includes everything from the earthly level up to Sadāśiva.

rows.grounds: the measure of all the worlds

items.question: How is the manifest range characterized and what topic is introduced next?
premises: All that manifest range is declared to be produced.
It is subject to arising and destruction.
Now the measure of all the worlds, as taught by the gurus, will be presented.
items.inference: The produced cosmos is impermanent, and the text now turns to the gurus' account of the worlds' measure.
items.plain_english: All that is declared to be produced and subject to arising and destruction. Now I will present the measure of all the worlds as it was taught to me by my own gurus.

items.question: What inner cosmic figures are listed at the start of the world-measure account?
premises: The account will be given briefly for understanding so one may quickly traverse it.
Within the cosmic egg are Ananta and Kāla.
Also present are Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.
items.inference: The world-measure summary begins by naming key figures inside the cosmic egg.
uncertainties: The verse bridges a general introduction and a list, so its syntax is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: That will now be explained briefly so that the mind may quickly move through it. Within the cosmic egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.

rows.grounds: having one hundred and eight worlds
in the group of seven: water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and root

items.question: How are the Rudras and the outer Nivṛtti worlds enumerated?
premises: There are one hundred Rudras together with their hosts.
Outside is Nivṛtti with one hundred and eight worlds.
These are distributed individually across the sevenfold group of water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and root.
items.inference: The verse gives a numerical placement of Rudras and Nivṛtti worlds within the lower tattva grouping.
uncertainties: The exact distribution implied by pratyekam across the sevenfold group is not fully spelled out in this verse.
items.plain_english: There are one hundred Rudras with their hosts. Outside is Nivṛtti, which has one hundred and eight worlds, distributed individually across the sevenfold group of water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and root.
